text:
The man is likely to prevail. When the woman conveyed the house to him, he owned both the dominant and servient parcels, so the easement was extinguished by merger. The purchaser can't claim an implied easement or one by necessity: the man never used the path while he owned both parcels, and the path was only a more direct route, not the only access. The warranty deed didn't create a new easement.

CONFIDENCE: 85
